# Wisp's patches to Ambiq's Zephyr fork (safety rule 8)

Ambiq's EM9305 driver erases and reflashes the BLE controller's NVM on its own: when the device version is older than or equal to the bundled `ble_fw_image_em9305.h`, when the version can't be read, and when the controller fails to boot ([safety.md](../../../../docs/wisp/safety.md) rule 8). Even ships its own EM9305 firmware, so that would wipe the radio. These patches take the ability away. They are not a runtime switch: the code is not in the image.

| Patch                                         | Project (west)                       | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hal_ambiq-0001-em9305-never-write-nvm.patch` | `ambiqhal_ambiq` @ `d3278ec`         | `am_devices_em9305.c`: the firmware update (`am_devices_em9305_update_fw`, erase, write, verify, version write), the NVM recovery reflash, configuration-mode entry and the HF crystal trim are compiled out behind `WISP_EM9305_NVM_WRITE`, which is an `#error` to define. `ble_fw_image_em9305.h` (the 234 KB controller image) is no longer included. `am_devices_em9305_init()` sets `skip_fw_update = true` for every caller and returns an error, instead of reflashing, when the controller does not come up. `CONFIG_BT_AMBIQ_EM9305_HF_CRYSTAL_CUSTOM_TRIM` is an `#error`. `am_devices_em9305.h`: the prototypes and the CM-PWM callback type go with them, so a caller that still uses them does not compile. |
| `zephyr-0001-em9305-never-write-nvm.patch`    | `zephyr` (`ambiqzephyr`) @ `89c8a36` | `drivers/bluetooth/hci/apollox_blue.c`: the HCI driver sets `.skip_fw_update = true`, no longer registers or drives the CM pad (configuration mode exists only for the update), and `bt_apollo_set_public_addr()` no longer sends vendor command `0xFC43` (whether it persists the address in the controller's NVM is undocumented; the controller keeps its own). `boards/ambiq/apollo510b_evb/board.c` (EXTREF init, not used by `wisp_g2`): `skip_fw_update = true` and no CM pad either.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

What stays: reset, the SPI transport, reading the firmware version (`HCI_VSC_READ_AT_ADDRESS`), the sleep option, and the vendor commands the HCI driver sends after every `HCI_Reset` (LE local features `0xFFF2`, TX power `0xFCC4`). Those configure the running controller; they are not documented as persistent either, see "Open" below.

## How they get applied, and why a build can't skip them

1. `pnpm nx run wisp-fw:setup` (`scripts/setup.sh`) runs `west update`, then applies every patch here that is not applied yet (`git apply`, idempotent). A patch that applies neither forwards nor backwards fails the setup: the pin moved and the patch must be redone.
2. `cmake/rule8.cmake`, at configure time of any Bluetooth build: each patch must be exactly in its project (`git apply --reverse --check`), else `WISP SAFETY RULE 8 … EM9305 patch missing`.
3. `scripts/check_rule8.py`, after every link of `wisp_g2`, proves the result on what was built: the compiled driver carries the patch marker; the driver and every caller, preprocessed with their exact compile commands, contain no update / recovery / NVM-write function, no `ble_fw_image_em9305.h` and none of the NVM write / erase / public-address opcodes, and every caller forces `skip_fw_update = true`; no such symbol, map section or instruction immediate is in the ELF; none of the controller image's bytes are in `zephyr.bin`.
4. `wisp-fw:test` proves 2 and 3 fire: configure fails against a pristine `hal_ambiq` and a pristine Zephyr (git worktrees of the pinned commits), and an image built from the pristine HAL with the configure check switched off (`WISP_RULE8_TEST_UNPATCHED`, test only) fails the post-build gate.

The patches carry Ambiq's code (Apache-2.0 / BSD-3-Clause) in diff context only. The EM9305 firmware image is in Ambiq's HAL repository, which west fetches into the git-ignored `.wisp-cache/`; it is never committed here, and the gates prove it is not linked.

## Moving the pin

Bump the revision in `west.yml`, run setup. If a patch no longer applies, redo it on the new tree (keep the same guard and the same `skip_fw_update` rule), regenerate it with `git diff` in that project, build, and run `wisp-fw:test`. Read the new `am_devices_em9305.c` in full first: a new NVM-writing path needs its own guard and an entry in `check_rule8.py`'s deny lists.

## Open

- Whether vendor commands `0xFFF2` (local LE features) and `0xFCC4` (TX power), which the HCI driver sends after each `HCI_Reset`, only touch the controller's RAM. Ambiq's driver sends them on every boot of their evb, which suggests runtime settings, but there is no public EM9305 command reference. They were not removed because without them the controller may advertise features the stack doesn't drive.
- Whether Even's EM9305 firmware boots without a patch load from the host. If it needs one, `am_devices_em9305_init()` now fails and Bluetooth stays off; nothing is written.
